about.text: Halloumi, or haloumi, is a type of dairy product made with milk originating from Cyprus. It is traditionally made from a mixture of goat milk and sheep's milk; however, due to lower cost of cow's milk and price sensitivity of consumers, modern halloumi increasingly contains cow's milk.

how.text: Cooking the curd in whey above 90 °C sets the protein so firmly that halloumi does not melt and can be grilled or fried; it is then folded with Cypriot mint leaves, giving its characteristic shape.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: Curd pieces are heated in the whey.

steps.name: fold
steps.note: Folded into rectangles or half-moons with Cypriot mint, 150–350 g each.

steps.name: salt
steps.note: The fresh type is salted with up to 3 % salt.
Only the mature type is kept, in salted whey of at most 6 % salt.
